extension.description: Scrobbles your Kodi playback to your self-hosted Chronicle server, and syncs ratings, artwork, and watch counts both ways. Chronicle is the source of truth for ratings and art (always pushed to Kodi); play counts and last-played dates reconcile in whichever direction has the more recent watch. Covers movies, movie collections, TV shows, and individual episodes. Supports resetting Kodi watch progress for a fresh rewatch while keeping your full history safe in Chronicle.
extension.news:
v2.3.3 - Code-review fixes to the Connect flow: device-auth network calls (initiate/QR download/poll) now have the same DNS-hang watchdog the sibling Chronicle_Scraper addons already had -- a dead/unreachable DNS server used to be able to hang Connect indefinitely with zero feedback; now it times out with an error instead. A QR pairing that was approved on the phone but whose one-time key never reached this device used to leave the QR window stuck open forever -- it now shows a clear error and asks you to try Connect again. The Settings status field could briefly flash back to "Not connected" immediately after a successful connect -- fixed. Declining the loopback-URL warning now actually cancels the connect instead of proceeding against that URL anyway. New "Change Chronicle URL" action (main menu and Settings) is the first way to correct a wrong URL once one is saved. A malformed response from Chronicle during device-auth now shows a specific error instead of crashing to a generic "Connect failed unexpectedly". v2.3.2 - v2.3.1 fixed _initiate()'s own cross-instance chronicle_url read but missed an identical one in _poll_loop() -- confirmed live against the sibling Chronicle_Scraper addons: after approving the device on the phone, the QR window never closed, since _poll_loop()'s own independent ADDON.getSetting('chronicle_url') read came back empty even though _initiate()'s POST (already fixed) had worked moments earlier. _poll_loop() now also uses self._base_url. v2.3.1 - Root cause of v2.3.0's URL-entry-still-not-working reports found via logging (same investigation against the sibling Chronicle_Scraper addons): confirmed live that default.py's own ADDON.setSetting('chronicle_url', ...) is not reliably visible to device_auth.py's SEPARATE xbmcaddon.Addon() instance's very next getSetting('chronicle_url') call -- same process, same addon, same settings.xml, one line apart, and still empty. DeviceAuthManager now takes the resolved URL as a constructor parameter instead of re-reading it independently. v2.3.0 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, per user request (same change applied to the sibling Chronicle_Scraper addons): the Chronicle URL now has exactly ONE entry point instead of two. Settings' own chronicle_url field is now read-only (enable="false") -- it was never reliably editable there to begin with. "Connect to Chronicle" is renamed "Edit Connection" and is now the only place a URL is ever entered: it prompts via a proven-reliable dialog ONLY when there isn't already a saved URL, so an already-connected reconnect skips straight to the QR window with no prompt -- a working URL is never typed twice. Also removed: the auto-bounce to Settings on first run, and all of v2.2.5-2.2.7's Action(Back)/reopen-Settings/settle-wait/fallback-prompt machinery -- none of it is necessary anymore now that Settings' text field is out of the picture entirely. v2.2.7 - Two fixes from a confirmed live report against the sibling Chronicle_Scraper addons: closing Settings (v2.2.6) did NOT fix it after all -- chronicle_url still read empty even after the dialog was fully closed, not just delayed. _initiate() now falls back to a single guaranteed-reliable xbmcgui.Dialog().input() prompt when chronicle_url is still empty after everything else has been tried, saves it explicitly, and proceeds -- only appears when the Settings-based path has actually failed. Also: the "Status" field in Settings was showing "Connected" purely because an api_key from a past successful connection was still saved, even while chronicle_url was empty -- _refresh_auth_status() now requires both, matching _is_configured()'s own check. v2.2.6 - Settings now reopens automatically right after v2.2.5's Action(Back) close (Addon.OpenSettings, non-blocking, unlike ADDON.openSettings()), so the forced close reads as a quick visual blip instead of dumping you back at whatever was behind Settings for the rest of the Connect flow -- Kodi's own window manager should restore focus to wherever you left off automatically. The QR window then appears on top of that reopened Settings screen. v2.2.5 - Root cause finally confirmed (same investigation against the sibling Chronicle_Scraper addons): chronicle_url was still at its empty default over a minute after the user typed a URL and could see it sitting in the field -- not a timing race (v2.2.4's settle-wait didn't help, because there was nothing to wait FOR), an ORDERING one. Kodi's addon Settings dialog only writes settings.xml to disk when the whole dialog closes, not per-field as focus moves between controls, and "Connect to Chronicle" is a button INSIDE that same still-open dialog. _connect_to_chronicle() now closes Settings first (Action(Back), only when Window.IsActive(addonsettings) confirms it's actually open -- a no-op from the main-menu path) before reading chronicle_url and connecting. v2.2.4 - Fixes the actual bug behind v2.2.1's (reverted) URL-confirm prompt, without bringing back the prompt -- same fix applied to Chronicle_Scraper. Confirmed live: chronicle_url read back completely empty immediately after typing a URL and clicking "Connect to Chronicle" from inside the still-open Settings dialog, for a URL that WAS saved correctly moments later. _initiate() now waits 500ms before its first read of chronicle_url, giving Kodi's Settings-dialog flush time to land -- fixes both a first-time URL entry and switching to a different URL, with no added dialog or retyping. v2.2.3 - BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: reverts v2.2.1's "confirm the URL before connecting" prompt -- same revert applied to Chronicle_Scraper, same reason: the new v2.2.2 logging caught it live, the prompt added a mandatory on-screen-keyboard URL retype to every single Connect attempt, and the actual bug report that led to this revert was the user backing out of that unexpected prompt within ~2 seconds, not a stale URL ever being used. "Connect to Chronicle" now goes straight to the QR window again, same as before v2.2.1. Diagnostic logging from v2.2.2 stays in place. v2.2.2 - Diagnostic logging only, no behavior change: the Connect flow (default.py's _connect_to_chronicle) now logs every step -- the URL read from disk, what the URL prompt returned, whether it changed, and DeviceAuthManager.run()'s own progress through _initiate()/QR-download/QRDialog construction/doModal(), plus a caught-and-logged traceback if anything in that call raises (a RunScript-launched script has no visible crash surface otherwise -- an unhandled exception would look identical to "the connection window just never showed up"). Added while investigating the same live report against the sibling Chronicle_Scraper addons. v2.2.1 - "Connect to Chronicle" now confirms the Chronicle URL directly (a text prompt, pre-filled with whatever's currently saved) instead of trusting chronicle_url on disk. Confirmed live (same fix applied to Chronicle_Scraper): switching URLs in Settings and immediately clicking "Connect to Chronicle" (the action button lives inside that same still-open Settings dialog) built the QR code against the OLD URL -- a just-typed text field's value isn't guaranteed to be flushed to settings.xml before Kodi launches the RunScript action as a brand new process. This also fixes the fresh-install case: opening the addon for the first time now prompts for the URL right in the Connect flow instead of requiring a value to already be saved before Connect can do anything with it. v2.2.0 - Three additions: (1) On-screen notifications when scrobbling starts and when an item is marked watched (new setting, "Show scrobble notifications", default on -- Scrobbling category). Previously this addon gave no visible sign it was doing anything at all. (2) "Connect to Chronicle" now shows the actual reason a connection attempt failed (empty URL, DNS failure, connection refused, timeout, HTTP error and its body) instead of the same generic "Could not contact the Chronicle server" for every failure -- same fix as Chronicle_Scraper's device_auth.py, same confirmed live complaint: identical text regardless of cause. (3) Writes a small signal file (special://temp/chronicle_scrobbler/) whenever a session crosses the watched threshold, for the new separate Chronicle Rating add-on (script.chronicle.rating) to pick up and prompt a SIMKL-style 1-10 rating from -- mirrors SIMKL's own split between its scrobbler and rating add-ons. Nothing changes here if that addon isn't installed; the signal files are just never consumed. v2.1.1 - Code review of v2.1.0's Player/Monitor split and resume feature turned up several real bugs, all fixed: (1) Kodi fires BOTH onPlayBackStarted and onAVStarted for video, so a session used to start twice, double-sending the opening scrobble and the resume lookup -- now guarded so only the first callback through starts a session. (2) The resume lookup was a blocking HTTP call made directly on Kodi's player-callback thread, which could stall Kodi for up to 10s if Chronicle was slow/unreachable -- moved to a background thread. (3) The opening scrobble could fire before a resume seek had actually taken effect (seekTime() isn't guaranteed synchronous), reporting a stale near-0% position right after telling Chronicle to resume elsewhere -- the opening scrobble is now skipped when a resume just happened, letting the next poll tick report the real post-seek position. (4) onSettingsChanged updated the shared client's URL and API key as two separate, unsynchronized writes, so a settings change mid-request could produce a request built from a mix of old and new values -- now a single atomic snapshot. (5) A malformed resume-lookup response could throw an uncaught exception out of the player callback, silently skipping the opening scrobble -- now validated defensively. (6) The poll thread and a Kodi callback (e.g. a seek) could both pass the scrobble-eligibility check before either recorded, sending duplicate scrobbles -- now guarded so only one send is in flight per session. Also collapsed 6 near-identical HTTP-request code paths in chronicle_client.py into one shared helper. v2.1.0 - CRITICAL FIX, confirmed live: this addon has never actually been able to send a single scrobble. ChronicleMonitor inherited only xbmc.Monitor while defining onPlayBackStarted/onAVStarted/onPlayBackPaused/onPlayBackResumed/onPlayBackStopped/onPlayBackEnded/onPlayBackSeek/onPlayBackError -- per Kodi's own docs, those are xbmc.Player callbacks, never delivered to a Monitor subclass, no matter what methods it defines with the same names. No exception, nothing in kodi.log -- Kodi's core simply never called them. Confirmed directly: a real playback session produced zero [monitor] log lines, while a different addon's own xbmc.Player subclass logged onAVStarted normally at the same moment. Since _on_start() (which begins a scrobble session) was only ever reachable from those callbacks, and the poll thread's own update no-ops without an active session, no scrobble could ever have gone out, regardless of Chronicle connectivity, API key, or any setting. Fixed by splitting into two classes: new ChroniclePlayer(xbmc.Player) now owns every playback callback and the actual scrobble-sending logic; ChronicleMonitor(xbmc.Monitor) keeps the system-level events (settings-changed, scan-finished) and the service's own poll thread, constructing and holding the ChroniclePlayer instance. Also fixed a related latent bug _send_update() had (masked by the same root cause, since it was never actually reached with should_scrobble() returning False in practice): the outer function referenced an unassigned payload variable whenever a poll tick wasn't yet due to scrobble.
Cross-device resume, the feature that surfaced the above: playback start now checks Chronicle for a resume position left by a DIFFERENT device (only when Kodi itself has no local resume bookmark of its own for the item -- a local bookmark always wins, since it can't be any staler than the last scrobble Chronicle received). Requires Chronicle server v0.9.0+ (adds POST /api/v1/scrobble/resume and UserLibrary.ResumePositionPercent, cleared once an item crosses the watched threshold). Also fixes a second real, previously-silent bug: to_scrobble_payload() has always sent mediaType="episode" for TV content (Kodi's own item type string), which the server's media-type matching never recognized as an alias for "tv" -- every TV episode scrobble/resume-lookup was failing to resolve a type. Fixed server-side (MediaItemMatcher.NormalizeMediaTypeName). v2.0.16 - Confirmed directly that Kodi's "Set Content" re-scan toggle does not clear the underlying video library database -- only a separate VideoLibrary.Clean operation does -- so stale entries (moved/renamed/deleted files) survived indefinitely no matter how many times a scan ran, automatic or manual. onScanFinished now runs VideoLibrary.Clean itself immediately after any video scan completes, throttled to at most once every 2 minutes so a normal scan-then-clean pair doesn't trigger a second redundant clean. v2.0.15 - The device name sent to Chronicle (shown on the phone's "Do you wish to connect X to Chronicle" approval screen) now prefers the machine's actual DNS/OS hostname over Kodi's own arbitrary FriendlyName setting, since that's a more verifiable identifier for which physical device is actually connecting. Falls back to the old "Kodi — FriendlyName" label if no usable hostname is available. v2.0.14 - Added a live countdown ("Expires in MM:SS", yellow, matching SIMKL's own device-auth screen) to the Connect to Chronicle dialog. Purely informational -- actual expiry is still decided server-side and detected via polling -- but previously there was no visible indication of how much time was left at all. v2.0.13 - Server-side device-auth code is now 6 characters (down from 32), used directly in a shortened verification URL (/a/<code> instead of /device-auth/<32-char-code>), and codes now last 15 minutes instead of 5, matching SIMKL. Approve/deny on an already-used or expired link now refreshes to the correct state instead of a generic error. Also added a confirmation prompt when the Chronicle URL is set to localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 -- easy to miss that this only works if Chronicle runs on the same device as Kodi. v2.0.12 - Fix (confirmed, self-tested via Kodi's JSON-RPC + screenshot rather than guessed): QR code actually renders now. Root cause was writing the downloaded file through Python's raw open() -- that puts real bytes on disk, but bypasses Kodi's own VFS layer entirely, so xbmcvfs.exists() on the exact same special://temp/... path returned False and ControlImage (which resolves through that same VFS layer) never found it. Switched to xbmcvfs.File() for the write. Cancel button also given no custom colors at all now -- it uses this Kodi skin's own native button/focus look instead of a fixed color, so it'll look right regardless of which skin is active. v2.0.11 - Fix: QR image still didn't render even with a confirmed-valid, uniquely-named, real-RGB PNG on disk. ControlImage was given the translatePath()-converted raw OS path (e.g. C:\Users\...\cache\...); Kodi's GUI/texture layer is documented to expect special:// VFS notation, which is how the addon's own bundled images (panel, buttons) were already being referenced and is exactly why those rendered fine while this didn't. Now passes the untranslated special://temp/... path to the dialog; translatePath() is still used internally only for Python's own file write. v2.0.10 - Fix: Cancel button on the connect dialog used unstyled Kodi skin defaults, rendering with poor contrast and text that didn't fit the box. Given explicit textures and white text color matching the rest of the dialog. (Companion server-side fix, not shipped in this zip: Chronicle's QR endpoint was still returning grayscale PNGs, not full RGBA -- Kodi's texture loader needed a real color-type conversion, not just a higher bit depth.) v2.0.9 - Fix: QR image still didn't show even after the server started returning a valid PNG. Every attempt downloaded to the same fixed filename (chronicle_qr.png); Kodi's texture manager caches loaded images by path for the session, so it kept showing whatever it first loaded there regardless of the file being overwritten on disk. Each attempt now downloads to a filename unique to its device-auth code. v2.0.8 - Fix: the QR connect dialog had no background at all -- WindowDialog is transparent by default and no control was ever drawn behind the text/QR image, so the Settings page underneath showed straight through, making both illegible. Added a dimmed full-screen backdrop plus an opaque card panel behind the dialog's own controls. v2.0.7 - Rebuilt Settings to match SIMKL Scrobbler's layout: Connection tab now leads with the Chronicle URL field followed directly by a "Connect to Chronicle" QR/PIN button and a read-only status line, so connecting never requires typing an API key by hand. settings.xml also switched to the classic flat schema (proven against SIMKL's own real, working settings.xml) instead of the newer section/group schema, since that's what supports an in-page action button. Unconfigured clicks go straight to this Settings page again, matching SIMKL's own first-run behavior. v2.0.6 - Fix: opening the addon once a URL was set but before connecting reopened Settings instead of the menu, making "Connect to Chronicle" unreachable without typing an API key by hand. The first-run check no longer also requires the key. Also flattened description/changelog text -- the XML source's line-wrapping indentation was being rendered literally in Kodi's add-on info screen. v2.0.5 - Fix: Chronicle URL field was silently missing from the Connection settings page (allowempty=false combined with an empty default made Kodi drop just that one setting). v2.0.4 - Fix: "This add-on can't be configured" when opening Settings (settings.xml used an unsupported schema variant). v2.0.3 - Fix: addon showed Kodi's generic fallback icon instead of the Chronicle "C" (icon.png wasn't declared via an <assets> block). v2.0.2 - Fix: opening the addon before it's configured now jumps straight to Settings instead of a menu that would only fail. v2.0.1 - Fix: removed the xbmc.gui dependency declaration, which isn't a real resolvable addon and broke every install. v2.0.0 - Bidirectional sync: ratings + art (Chronicle -> Kodi, source of truth) and play count / last-played reconciliation for movies, movie collections, TV shows, and episodes. v1.1.0 - QR code device authentication; sync Chronicle lists to Kodi playlists v1.0.0 - Initial release
